title: Ampleness of regular dominant flag line bundles
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and with every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group having finite central kernel an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ (a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup), with character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$ and integer coroot pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Here a split maximal torus is a maximal subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$. Write $p:B\to T$ for the projection with kernel the unipotent radical and put $Q=S/B$. For $\mu\in X$ put $\widetilde\mu=\mu\circ p$ and $M_\mu=\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\mu}$ [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], the invertible sheaf associated to the quotient action $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\widetilde\mu(b)z)$. The scheme $Q$ is a smooth projective geometrically integral $F$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme]. For every $\mu\in X$ with $\langle\mu,\alpha^\vee\rangle>0$ for all $\alpha\in\Delta$, the invertible sheaf $M_\mu$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The assertion includes the trivial group: the inequalities are vacuous, $Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $M_0=\mathcal O_Q$ is ample.

source.place: Part II, section 4, flag-line geometry (exact ampleness location to be checked), WANTED. Milne iAG2017 22.49--22.51, printed p.480, explains the geometric input. Online corroboration read: Mathieu, Tilting Modules and their Applications, AS Pure Math 26 (2000), proof of Theorem 3.2, printed p.158, assertions (i)--(ii), https://www.imsc.res.in/~knr/vdk/mathieu.pdf. These give the needed M_(lambda+rho) and M_(lambda+2rho); regular dominance is the general ample-cone formulation.

proof.text: The group $S$ is reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Apply [lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry] to this pair: $Q$ is smooth and projective. The latter notion includes quasi-compactness by [def-pc-projective-morphism]. By [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts], $Q$ is geometrically integral; its open big cell $C=Un_0B/B$ is affine space, and finitely many translates of $C$ cover $Q$. This establishes the geometric clause independently of ampleness.

source.place: Theorem 17.9, Theorem 21.73 and Remark 21.74; projectivity convention: Stacks Tag 01W8

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-simply-connected-character-lattice], write $\mu=\sum_{i=1}^r a_i\omega_i$, where $a_i=\langle\mu,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle$. The assumed strict inequalities make every $a_i$ a positive integer. This is an equality in the actual character lattice, including in positive characteristic.

Use [lem-sfb-fundamental-flag-boundary-sections] to choose $s_i\in\Gamma(Q,M_{\omega_i})$ whose zero loci exhaust the individual boundary components of $C$. This input concerns fundamental sections and their supports; it makes no ampleness assertion for those individual bundles.

source.place: Remark 22.49, printed p.480; Brion--Kumar Exercises 2.2.E(2)--(3), printed pp.70--71

proof.text: The characteristic-line map $c_B$ is a homomorphism by [lem-sfb-borel-characteristic-picard-sequence], so $M_\mu\simeq\bigotimes_iM_{\omega_i}^{\otimes a_i}$. The signs agree: $M_\nu=c_B(-\nu\circ p)$. Form the tensor section $s=\bigotimes_i s_i^{\otimes a_i}$ and carry it to $M_\mu$ using this isomorphism. In a local frame at any $x$, its coefficient is $\prod_i f_i^{a_i}$, where $f_i$ is the coefficient of $s_i$. A product in a local ring is a unit exactly when every factor is a unit; since every $a_i>0$, this gives $Q_s=\bigcap_i Q_{s_i}=C$. Thus $Q_s$ is affine. For $r=0$ the character lattice is zero, $M_0=\mathcal O_Q$, the empty tensor section is $1$, and the same equality is $Q_1=C=Q$.

source.place: Theorem 18.15 (128), printed p.390; local unit calculation, Stacks Properties Definition 01PS

proof.text: The homogeneous line bundle in [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections] has left $S$-action $h[g,z]=[hg,z]$. This is well-defined because left multiplication commutes with $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\widetilde\mu(b)z)$; its inverse for fixed $h\in S(F)$ is left multiplication by $h^{-1}$. It carries $s$ to the global section $(h s)(x)=h\bigl(s(h^{-1}x)\bigr)$ of the same $M_\mu$. At every point the fibre map is invertible, so $Q_{h s}=hQ_s=hC$. The finite translates in step 1 therefore give an affine nonvanishing cover by sections of $M_\mu$ itself. Since $Q$ is quasi-compact, [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] applies with exponent $1$ at every point. Hence $M_\mu$ is ample. For the trivial group the quotient is $\operatorname{Spec}F$ and the section $1$ of $\mathcal O_Q$ already gives this cover.

source.place: Section 18c and Remark 22.49; Stacks properties.tex Definition 01PS (definition-ample)
